working_title: The Market Is Growing. So Why Do You Feel Broke?
audience_tension: Headline growth and rising markets can coexist with a household experience of falling room to breathe.
lived_contradiction: The dashboard says the economy and asset market grew, while rent food debt service and the distance to ownership still feel harder.
popular_explanation: The popular answer reduces the experience to unusually high inflation or interest rates and assumes the same conditions reach everyone similarly.
missing_mechanism: Research must test how asset ownership income growth debt exposure housing costs and market concentration distribute nominal growth across households.
thesis: Does the gap between asset-owner compounding and household cash-flow growth explain more of the lived contradiction than the headline growth rate alone?
distribution_question: Who owns the assets producing the measured gains, who receives the income, and which households carry the rising recurring costs?
countercase: Broad wage gains employment access transfers and falling inflation may improve household conditions even when wealth and asset gains remain unequal.
failure_conditions: The selected household data do not show a meaningful ownership or cash-flow distribution gap.
Headline inflation and rates explain the measured experience better after controlling for income and housing tenure.
plain_language_translation: A rising tide can lift the boats that are already in the water while people still standing on the dock pay more to get in.
visual_metaphor: A market elevator rises behind three households while ownership tickets cash-flow drains and debt weights determine who can enter each floor.
